title: Measures to Reduce Incidence of Mass Food Poisoning
what_it_is: Measures to Reduce Incidence of Mass Food Poisoning

sections.label: Mass food poisoning and food safety
sections.summary: Questions ask the causes of November 2018 mass food poisoning and what Government will do on safe food handling standards, penalties, suspensions and technology.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) what are the causes of the spate of mass food poisoning incidents in November 2018; and (b) what will the Government do to heighten awareness of and compliance to safe food handling standards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) whether there is an assessment on whether the current measures and penalties in place have been efficient in improving food safety; (b) what is the total number of food establishments and caterers whose licences have been suspended for failing a hygiene inspection in the past five years and the breakdown of the number for each year; and (c) whether technology has been adopted to equip inspectors in carrying out their jobs more efficiently and effectively.

sections.label: Spize Restaurant licence terminated
sections.summary: The operating licence of Spize Restaurant at River Valley Road was terminated and NEA will press charges against the operator in Court.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The operating licence of Spize Restaurant at River Valley Road was terminated and NEA will also press charges against the operator in Court.

sections.label: Penalties for unfit food
sections.summary: Operators selling food unfit for human consumption may face up to $10,000 for a first offence, and repeat offenders $20,000, three months' imprisonment, or both.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For selling food that is found unfit for human consumption, operators may face a penalty of up to $10,000 for the first offence and, in the case of repeat offenders, a fine of $20,000, or imprisonment of three months, or both.

sections.label: Consumer food safety advice
sections.summary: Consumers are urged to use only licensed caterers, eat catered food within the stated consume-by period, and report poor hygiene practices to authorities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Consumers are urged to engage only licensed caterers and consume catered food within the stipulated "consume by" time period.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Consumers who come across poor hygiene practices in food establishments should provide feedback to the authorities for further investigation.

sections.label: Food caterer inspections numbers
sections.summary: For food caterers, 2,400 inspections were done plus 900 since last month, and 77,000 inspections were done in 2018, including unannounced ones.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As I have said for last year, for food caterers, we have actually done 2,400 inspections, in addition to 900 inspections since last month, and this is actually not all.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For the whole of 2018, they have actually done 77,000 inspections, not just for licence renewal, but unannounced inspections.

sections.label: Food handler training requirement
sections.summary: All food handlers must undertake and complete the basic food hygiene course and be registered before handling food at licensed premises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Indeed, with regard to training, all food handlers have to undertake and complete the basic food hygiene course, and then to be registered before they can be allowed to handle food at these licensed premises.

sections.label: Food hygiene officer requirements
sections.summary: Licensed premises must have a food hygiene officer and food safety management system, and from 21 December 2018 suspended premises must have their FHOs retrained and recertified under the WSQ course.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We require them to have a food hygiene officer, as well as implement a food safety management system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: That is the reason why from 21 December 2018, we require any licensed premises that are suspended to get their FHOs to train again and be recertified under the WSQ course.
